item.title: Version 0.4.0
item.description:
Smorza 0.4.0
- A welcome window explains the one permission before macOS asks for it - Actions for the Shortcuts app, and smorza:// links for Terminal and Raycast - Shortcuts to open the mixer and to turn the playing app up, down or mute it - Ignore an app: Smorza leaves its sound alone and stops listing it - A Notifications & alerts row for the system alert volume - The menu bar icon shows Mute All, and the output volume if you like - Sliders in each app's colour, and Liquid Glass on macOS 26 - German, French and Croatian - The volume keys now change the playing app instead of the app in front
If you use the volume keys, macOS may ask for Accessibility again after this update.

item.title: Version 0.3.0
item.description:
Smorza 0.3.0
- A settings window behind the gear in the panel - The volume keys can change the app in front; Option + the keys still change the Mac's volume - Scroll over a row to change its volume, and move a focused slider with the arrow keys - Pin an app to keep it in the list while it is quiet, so you can set it before it plays - Mute All, from the panel or with Control-Option-M anywhere - An output priority list: the first connected device becomes the output, and each device keeps its own volume - A small overlay when the output changes
If you use the volume keys, macOS may ask for Accessibility again after this update.

item.title: Version 0.2.1
item.description:
Smorza 0.2.1, the first release under the new name (formerly Volume Mixer).
- An output device for each app: Spotify on the speakers, Discord in the AirPods - Level meters under the apps that go through the mixer, while the panel is open - Updates itself from now on: checks once a day and asks before installing - Turned-down apps reach the speakers 10 ms sooner (12 ms instead of 23 ms) - The app opens at once instead of waiting on macOS's audio service - An aggregate device that includes a microphone works as an output - Copy Diagnostics: right-click the version at the bottom of the panel
Coming from Volume Mixer: Smorza takes over your volumes and devices on its first launch. macOS asks for the audio permission once more, because the app has a new name.
